name: Gmail
summary: Google's mail service, for personal @gmail.com addresses and for custom domains through Google Workspace, with Calendar and Contacts attached.

factors: An @gmail.com address belongs to Google and cannot move with you
'Sign in with Google' ties dozens of other accounts to this one
Labels, filters and search habits built up over years
Calendar sharing and meeting invitations inside the Google ecosystem

export.summary: Mail exports as a standard mbox file or syncs out over IMAP. Calendars and contacts export in open formats. The address itself is what you cannot take.

methods.name: Google Takeout
methods.detail: Exports all mail as mbox, calendars as .ics and contacts as vCard.

methods.name: IMAP sync
methods.detail: imapsync, or your new server's own sync jobs, copies mail directly to the new mailbox. Use an app password or OAuth. Google throttles IMAP downloads, so a large mailbox takes days.

caveats: With an @gmail.com address, set up forwarding and change your address everywhere gradually; keep the account alive for at least a year
Labels become folders, so a message with three labels can be copied three times unless your tool deduplicates
Before closing the account, change every 'Sign in with Google' login to a password or passkey
Filters export as an XML file that only Gmail understands; recreate the important ones

paths.verdict: A good first step: move to a client you control while the mailbox stays where it is.

import.summary: Add the account and sign in with Google; mail, calendars and address books sync. To take mail out of Google altogether, copy folders into Thunderbird's Local Folders or import the Takeout mbox.

transfers: All mail, with labels shown as folders
Several accounts in one unified inbox
lost: Gmail's search speed and automatic categories
Conversation view exactly as Gmail does it

paths.verdict: For a domain you own, when someone is willing to take on running mail properly.

import.summary: Create the mailboxes and add a sync job for each Gmail account; mailcow pulls the mail over IMAP in the background. Import calendars and contacts into SOGo, then switch the MX records.

lost: Gmail's spam filtering quality and its sending reputation
Gmail filters, which need recreating as Sieve rules
An @gmail.com address, if that is what you use

paths.verdict: A lean, modern server for technically confident people who are happy with standard mail clients.

import.summary: Create the accounts, copy mail across with imapsync, import calendars and contacts over CalDAV and CardDAV, then switch the MX records.

lost: Gmail's spam filtering quality and its sending reputation
Gmail filters, which need recreating as Sieve rules
An @gmail.com address, if that is what you use
